'''Shaul Reuven Foguel''' ({{langx|he| שאול פוגל}}, December 5, 1931 - December 19, 2020) was an Israeli mathematician. Shaul Foguel was born to one of the founding families of the City of [[Tel Aviv]]<ref>Who killed Abraham Fogel 70 years ago?https://www.haaretz.co.il/misc/1.1270464</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.geni.com/projects/Founders-of-Tel-Aviv-Ahuzat-Bayit/5620|title=Founders of Tel Aviv|website=Geni|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-11}}</ref> and his mother Dora Malkin was a direct descendant of [[Saul Wahl]].<ref>Interview with Shaul Foguel, Nov 26, 2015</ref> He received his B.S. and M.S. in Mathematics from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] and his PhD in Mathematics from [[Yale University]] in 1958. He wrote his dissertation under [[Nelson Dunford]] on "Studies in Spectral Operators and the Basis Problem". Shaul Foguel was Professor Emeritus of the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], and a supporter of the Israeli Left. He ran in the [[1969 Israeli legislative election|1969 Knesset elections]] on the Peace List along with [[Gadi Yatziv]], although it failed to win a seat. He spent his retirement in [[New York City]], where his two sons, [[Tuval Foguel|Professor Tuval Foguel]] of [[Adelphi University]], and Sy Foguel, the CEO of [[Berkshire Hathaway GUARD Insurance Companies]] live.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.guard.com/management.htm|title = Leadership | date=24 March 2019 }}</ref>

==Publications==
* Shaul R. Foguel "Selected topics in the study of Markov operators" Dept. of Mathematics, [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], 1980
* Shaul R. Foguel "The Ergodic theory of Markov processes" Van Nostrand Reinhold Co., 1969
